key_insight: MetaboNet consolidates multiple public Type 1 Diabetes datasets into the largest standardized, easy-to-use resource to accelerate fair, comparable algorithm development for T1D management.
problem_solved: Existing T1D datasets are fragmented, inconsistent in format and annotation, and time-consuming to integrate, which hampers reproducibility, benchmarking, and generalization of AI models.
method: Aggregate publicly available T1D datasets and map them to a unified schema with consistent timestamps, variable names, units, and clinical labels.
Apply standardized preprocessing and quality-control pipelines (missing data handling, alignment of sensor/insulin/nutrition signals, provenance metadata) to produce analysis-ready cohorts.
Provide documentation and tooling for easy access, reproducible splits, and interoperable formats to enable benchmarking and downstream ML workflows.
impact: By removing data wrangling barriers and providing a single, well-documented resource, MetaboNet enables faster, more reproducible development and fair comparison of T1D management algorithms across research groups.
visual_elements: Overview diagram: multiple heterogeneous dataset icons funneling into a single standardized MetaboNet repository (before/after consolidation).
Schema map: example unified record showing aligned fields—timestamp, glucose, insulin, carbs, activity, metadata—with color-coded harmonization.
Quality/coverage chart: bar or heatmap comparing variable availability and cohort size across source datasets vs. consolidated MetaboNet.
Workflow icon strip: data ingestion → cleaning & harmonization → analysis-ready dataset → model benchmarking (icons for each stage).
paper_title: MetaboNet: The Largest Publicly Available Consolidated Dataset for Type 1 Diabetes Management
paper_authors: Miriam K. Wolff, Peter Calhoun, Eleonora Maria Aiello, Yao Qin, Sam F. Royston
